title: Here Are the Winners of the 2026 BET Awards: Updating Live
summary: Teyana Taylor is owning 'Culture's Biggest Night.'
contentText:
Teyana Taylor is among the big winners at the 2026 BET Awards, which are being held at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Sunday, June 28. The show, hosted by  Druski , is airing live at 8 p.m. ET/PT on BET and will be simulcast on BET HER, CMT, LOGO, MTV, MTV2, Nickelodeon (NAN), Paramount, POP, VH1, Comedy Central and TV Land.

In addition to receiving the Icon of the Year award, Taylor won three competitive awards – best actress, video director of the year and the fashion vanguard award, a new award this year. Taylor has had a year for the record books, winning a Golden Globe and receiving an Oscar nomination for One Battle After Another, and receiving a Grammy nomination for best R&B album for Escape Room .

In the best actress category, Taylor bested last year’s winner, Cynthia Erivo, as well as the 2023 winner Angela Bassett, among others.

Clipse ’s Let God Sort ‘Em Out won album of the year. The LP was nominated for album of the year and best rap album at the Grammy Awards in February but didn’t win in either category. Clipse’s album beat the latest by two artists who had previously won in this category at the BET Awards – Cardi B and Bruno Mars (who had won with his Silk Sonic project).

Leon Thomas won best male R&B/pop artist for the first time, beating, among others, three repeat past winners in this category: Chris Brown, who has won a record eight times; Usher, who has won five times; and Bruno Mars, who has won three times. Thomas won two Grammys: best R&B album for Mutt and best traditional R&B performance for “Vibes Don’t Lie.”

Kehlani won best female R&B/pop artist for the first time, beating, among others, SZA, who won in the category the last three years. Kehlani won two Grammys: best R&B song and best R&B performance, both for her soulful ballad “Folded.”

Cardi B won best female hip-hop artist. It’s her third win in the category; her first since she won back-to-back awards in 2018-19.

In addition to Taylor, two other ground-breaking women are set to receive special awards. Ms. Lauryn Hill will be honored with the inaugural Living Legend Icon Award. Legendary music executive Sylvia Rhone will be named the recipient of the Ultimate Icon Award.

Jazzy’s World TV won the rising star award. That’s the stage name of Jazlyn Guerra, 16, a budding journalist who conducts unstructured interviews of celebrities. Raised in New York City, she first gained recognition for her interview with Jay-Z in 2021. Since then, she has interviewed more rappers (Kendrick Lamar, Cardi B, Lil Uzi Vert, J. Cole, Nicki Minaj, Lil Wayne), singers (Alicia Keys), actors (Denzel Washington, Tom Holland), comedians (Steve Harvey), athletes (Shaquille O’Neal, Carmelo Anthony), politicians (Kamala Harris, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez) and more. Past winners in the category include Keke Palmer, Jaden & Willow Smith and Blue Ivy Carter.

Connie Orlando, EVP, specials, music programming & music strategy at BET, serves as executive producer for the 2026 BET Awards. Jesse Collins Entertainment is the production company for the show, with Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon, and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay also serving as executive producers.
